lead: Iowa plumbing deals with cold winters, basements, hard water and river flooding. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across the state.
risk: frozen pipes, flooded basements and hard water scale
risk_short: frozen pipes, flooding and hard water
why: Iowa water is hard in most areas, so softeners are common and scale wears out water heaters and fixtures. Many homes have basements with sump pumps.
River flooding has hit Cedar Rapids, Des Moines and other towns, and heavy rain backs up sewers. Winters freeze pipes. The Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board licenses plumbers.
tips: Test your sump pump before spring.
Keep your softener supplied with salt.
areas: Calls come from Des Moines, Cedar Rapids, Davenport, Sioux City, Iowa City, Waterloo, Ames and rural Iowa.

faq.a: In most areas, yes. Hard water leaves scale on fixtures and in water heaters. A water test shows your hardness and helps size a softener.
